newsitem.title: GERMANY: Union participating in Krupp/Thyssen talks.
newsitem.headline: Union participating in Krupp/Thyssen talks.

text.p: A union representative participating in talks between industrial groups Krupp and Thyssen was pressing the companies to rule out layoffs if the firms agree to form a joint steel company, the IG Metall union said on Monday.
Large-scale layoffs would be met with "the most massive opposition" by IG Metall, which has thousands of workers at both Thyssen AG and Fried. Krupp AG Krupp-Hoesch.

The union planned to demonstrate against possible job cuts as the two companies continue negotiations stemming from a hostile takeover bid Krupp launched last week. Harald Schartau, a member of the union and the Krupp supervisory board, was participating in the talks.

IG Metall also said on Monday it would oppose any merger that embraced a Krupp cost-cutting plan to eliminate 2,200 of 10,000 jobs in its steel subsidiary, Krupp Stahl AG. Krupp announced those cuts in February before bidding for Thyssen.
